title: PySpark chained transformations on a single column
question:
WithColumn functions are considered expensive, and therefore, select statements are generally encouraged when modifying multiple columns. But what if we want to chain various transformations for a single column?

df.withColumn("name", lower(col("name")))
  .withColumn("name", regexp_replace(col("name"), r"[,.]", ""))
  .withColumn("name", trim(col("name")))
  .withColumn(...)
  .withColumn(...)

This seems likely to quickly get out of hand as the number of transformations increases.

Is nesting the expressions the convention?:

df.withColumn("name", trim(regexp_replace(lower(col("name")), r"[,.]", "")))

Or does PySpark provide cleaner solutions for such cases?
answer:
Let's test it by using an example:

df = spark.createDataFrame([(" Hi, I'am J ", )], schema=["name"])

By using your first block of code, the physical execution plan will be:

== Physical Plan ==
*(1) Project [trim(regexp_replace(lower(name#2), [,.], , 1), None) AS name#8]
+- *(1) Scan ExistingRDD[name#2]

If we use your second expression, the physical plan will be:

== Physical Plan ==
*(1) Project [trim(regexp_replace(lower(name#2), [,.], , 1), None) AS name#15]
+- *(1) Scan ExistingRDD[name#2]

Both give the same execution plan and result:

+---------+
|name     |
+---------+
|hi i'am j|
+---------+

In the execution perspective, Spark optimizer have already optimized the execution plan for you no matter which style are you using.
